title: The store facade is the only module that talks to the underlying engine
asA: developer who needs the engine to be swappable and the domain to be testable against a double
iWant: one module to hold the engine binding and expose named verbs, with no consumer importing the engine directly
soThat: the boundary between the domain and the engine is the only place that has to move when the engine changes and the only place tests have to mock

acceptanceCriteria.description: Exactly one source-tree module imports the engine binding. Every other module that touches persistence imports the store facade.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the running source tree after boot
acceptanceCriteria.when: the import graph is inspected for uses of the engine binding module
acceptanceCriteria.then: the engine binding is imported by exactly one file (the store facade) and no other file in the source tree imports it, verified by an import-graph query or a targeted grep

acceptanceCriteria.description: The facade exposes named verbs for every persistence operation the domain requires; it does not expose a general-purpose query method that accepts raw engine-native queries from consumers.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every exported function has a domain-shaped name and typed parameters (not a raw query string parameter), and no exported function accepts an engine-native query object or raw SQL string as a call argument from consumer code

acceptanceCriteria.description: Replacing the facade with an in-memory double that implements the same verb surface allows the domain code to run against it without importing the engine binding.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a test double implementing the same named verbs as the facade with an in-memory backing store
acceptanceCriteria.when: the domain code runs against the double in place of the facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the domain code executes to completion without importing the engine binding at any point in its call path and its behaviour is unchanged from a facade-backed run for the operations under test
